messages:
alex: Hi team — incoming escalation from Acme. They hit a big marketing blast at 11:02 UTC, our Dedicated pool started returning 429s and latency spiked to 1.2s/token for the gen-model. Customer reports ~30% errors and timeouts. Can we triage?
prod-monitor-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool-prod-7 high token/s (p95 3.2k tps), throttles increased, burst_credits remaining=0, autoscaler did not add GPUs (policy=staged, headroom=10%).
jane_acme: @alex seeing a bunch of 429s and slow responses. This is causing page outages for us. Please advise asap.
alex: Thanks @jane_acme — sorry for the outage. Adding infra. @maria @ben can you start with pool id and model variant? Also capture request ids for the 429s if possible.
maria: Joining. Pool: dedicated-prod-7, model: redwood-4b-ops-v2 (fp16/8bit-qt). Autoscale policy: min=2 GPUs, max=8, scale_up_step=1, target_util=70%. From metrics I see token/s on a single node peaked at ~3.2k and node GPU util hit 96% for ~4m. Burst credits chest drained to 0 at 11:05.
ben: I grabbed a couple logs. Repro snippet for one request that got 429: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model":"redwood-4b-ops-v2",
  "input":"<marketing prompt...>",
  "max_tokens":1024
}
```
Response: 429 {"error":"token_throttled","retry_after":2} and downstream latencies ~1.1s/token before throttle.
sam_ops: Two potential vectors: noisy neighbor (long-context high-token jobs from another tenant) or admission control mis-config (burst credits unexpected zero). Quick mitigation: 1) apply per-customer TPS cap in admission controller, 2) temporarily bump pool to +2 GPUs (emergency scale), 3) route Acme to a reserved slot or fallback smaller model.
maria: I cross-checked other tenants — one tenant had a batch job that started at 10:55 and was sending large streaming generation with ~1500 tokens per request at ~20 rps. That saturated KV cache and continued-batching windows, causing tail latency. Looks noisy-neighbory.
alex: OK. Actions: immediate (0-15m) and mid-term (1-7d). Immediate: (a) enable emergency scale to +2 GPUs for dedicated-prod-7, (b) enable per-tenant TPS cap to 600 tps, (c) route Acme to fallback model redwood-2b-ops with note to customer. Mid-term: revisit headroom policy and burst credit top-offs.
ben: Applied per-tenant cap rule (600 tps) in admission controller, added routing rule for Acme to fallback model; started emergency scale — new GPUs should come up in ~4m. Also added a temporary admission-control log to capture token-rate by API key.
prod-monitor-bot: UPDATE: dedicated-prod-7 GPUs increased to 4. Burst credits still 0, token/s dropped to 850 (post-cap), p99 latency decreased to 320ms/token. Throttles reduced.
jane_acme: Thanks @alex @ben — errors largely stopped for us, latency much improved. Appreciate the quick fix.
sam_ops: For RCA: we need to confirm why autoscaler didn't add nodes before burst credits hit 0. Hypothesis: staged policy with step 1 and cooldown prevented scale before saturation. Also burst credits zeroing should trigger emergency autoscale in policy.
maria: Agreed. From autoscaler logs: scale decision evaluated every 30s, but the target_util metric is computed across pool. The noisy job spiked individual node util while the average stayed below 70% until several nodes hit 95%. Our headroom=10% is too tight for these spike patterns.
alex: Good notes. For postmortem we should include: timeline, offending tenant id, token/sec curves per node, admission control decisions, burst_credit drains, autoscaler decisions + cooldown, and proposed config changes.
ben: Repro steps in staging to validate changes: 1) deploy staged autoscale config with headroom=25% and emergency_scale_threshold=90% -> step=2, cooldown=30s. 2) create a synthetic noisy neighbor: clients that send 1500-token requests at 20rps for 6m to a single model variant. 3) run Acme-like burst at 2.5k tps. Confirm that admission control caps and emergency-scale keep p99 < 500ms and throttles < 1%. I'll attach a k6 script in the issue.
sam_ops: Also recommend a feature: burst credit allocation per-customer vs per-pool. Right now credits are pool-level so a single noisy tenant can exhaust shared credits — that's a big pain for Dedicated customers. Add to roadmap.
maria: From billing side — Acme mentioned unexpected charges because of emergency GPU spin-up. @alex please coordinate with sales to offer a credit for the spin-up period; we'll tag it in the incident.
alex: Will do. Final immediate follow-ups: ben to post k6 repro + logs, maria to open autoscaler config PR to increase headroom and add emergency trigger, sam to draft admission-control per-customer cap guideline, and I'll draft incident update for Acme + credit proposal.
ben: Posted k6 script and initial staging run results in the incident ticket #INC-9842. With staged config (headroom=25%) the staging run maintained p99 < 420ms and throttles 0.3% at peak.
alex: Great. After the RCA we'll schedule a postmortem and reach out to Acme with a writeup. Thanks everyone — leaving this thread open for any more traces or customer details. :white_check_mark:
